newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Iri names Lehman Brothers Seat advisor.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Iri names Lehman Brothers Seat advisor.

text.p: Italian state industrial holding company IRI on Thursday appointed Lehman Brothers as advisor for the planned sale of Seat, the yellow pages publishing division of state telecoms group Stet.
IRI, which controls Stet, has said it wants to spin-off Seat by the end of the year. Stet is slated for privatisation in February or March 1997.
Newspapers say the government hopes that Seat will sell for around three trillion lire, of which 1.4 trillion would go to IRI, which holds some 46.5 percent of Stet's total capital.

IRI said earlier this month that it expects to seek a bourse listing for Seat, with ordinary and savings shares given to Stet shareholders in the same proportion as the respective stakes in Stet's capital.
The government is also pressing for IRI to consider selling off Stet units cable-layer Sirti and switchgear maker Italtel.

The chairman of IRI, Michele Tedeschi, said in a newspaper interview on Thursday that a long-awaited watchdog authority for Stet would have to be set up by November if the privatisation timetable for Stet was going to be respected.
He said IRI would need three months following the establishment of the watchdog to complete the sell-off process.

A government's bill on a telecoms watchdog is currently going through parliament, but is tied to disputed legislation on television ownership which could snarl passage of the package. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
